title: Hepatitis B vaccine
what: A vaccine shot that protects the liver from the hepatitis B virus. Usually several shots are needed on a schedule.
why: For newborns in the first days of life, children on the schedule, unvaccinated adults, health workers, and people with a family member who carries the virus.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes; the course is usually 3 shots over a few months
tell_doctor: If you are ill now or have a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are well. You will be checked first.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: The course is usually 3 shots. Write down the dates so you do not miss one.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that makes it easy to uncover your upper arm.

steps: The doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped, and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in your documents
After the shot, sit in the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes soreness at the spot for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes tiredness or a mild fever
after: Stay near the room for 30 minutes
You can go back to normal activities
Next shot on schedule. You will be given the date
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services

faq.q: What if I missed the second shot?
faq.a: The course usually does not need to start over. See your doctor, and they will continue from where you left off.

faq.q: Should I check my protection after the course?
faq.a: Sometimes an antibody test is advised, for example for health workers. Ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Hepatitis B vaccine tomorrow. Bring your vaccination record.
